name: AMD Radeon Pro VII product page (archived AMD page) - FP16/FP32/FP64/INT8 figures, dense, no structured-sparsity label
publisher: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD page, retrieved via the Wayback Machine)
notes: SUPERSEDED 2026-10-05 - THE NEGATIVE FINDING IN THIS RECORD WAS WRONG. Its central claim - that the cited page 'contains NO TFLOPS figure, NO "Peak ... Performance" specification row', with 'a regex sweep for "sparsit", "TFLOPS", "TFLOP", "TOPS" and "Peak " over the full extracted text of 18,346 characters returned ZERO matches' - is false. The page does carry a full GPU Specifications table. Re-read 2026-10-05 it yields, verbatim: 'Peak Single Precision (FP32) Performance 13.1 TFLOPs', 'Peak Double Precision (FP64) Performance 6.5 TFLOPs', 'Memory Size 16 GB', 'Memory Type (GPU) HBM2', 'Memory Interface 4096-bit', 'Memory Bandwidth Up to 1024 GB/s', 'Memory ECC Support Yes', 'Stream Processors 3840', 'Compute Units 60', 'Lithography TSMC 7nm FinFET', 'TBP 250W'. The tell is internal: a sweep for the literal token 'Peak ' that returns ZERO matches on a page whose most prominent heading is 'Specifications' is a failed probe, not an absence - and the record's own text said as much, noting the stored 13.1 was 'widely attributed to AMD' and 'should be treated as unestablished' while citing this very page for it. FOUR INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATIONS that the figures are present: (1) full spec table located in a plain web_extract of the archived URL (22,831 characters); (2) keyword sweep giving TFLOPs x2, Peak x2, 'sparsit' x0, 'TOPS' x0; (3) per-value regex, one occurrence each of '13.1', '1024', '4096'; (4) reading the contiguous table text. The sparsity sub-question is settled too, and negatively in AMD's favour: the page has NO sparsity footnote and NO row titled for structured sparsity, so its single printed figure is dense and must not be halved. SUPERSEDED BY w5a-part2-amd-radeon-pro-vii-page-does-contain-the-figure, which quotes the table. The record is kept and marked deprecated rather than deleted, because a wrong negative that was acted on is worth more as a visible correction than as a silent removal.
